source_spans.locator: Psychophysiology 44(4), published p.491, Abstract: reviewed time-resolved studies support context-based anticipation of likely upcoming features; anticipatory processing can carry costs, varies with age, and differs across hemispheric processing modes

Psychophysiology 44(4), published pp.492-493, Integration and Prediction / Figure 1: expected completions and equally unexpected within- versus between-category violations distinguish feature preactivation from post hoc contextual fit

Psychophysiology 44(4), published pp.493-494, anticipatory feature evidence: contextual information can preactivate semantic/conceptual, morpho-syntactic, and lexical/perceptual properties of not-yet-presented items; article/adjective responses can reflect properties of an expected later noun

Psychophysiology 44(4), published pp.494-495, prediction-cost section: unexpected unrelated completions after strongly constraining contexts elicit a later frontal positive response beyond the earlier expectancy-related response; suppression/revision interpretation remains tentative

Psychophysiology 44(4), published pp.495-497, Aging Effects / Figure 2: older adults as a group retain contextual-fit effects but show little prediction-specific facilitation; individual older adults with higher verbal fluency can show younger-like patterns

Psychophysiology 44(4), published pp.497-500, hemispheric visual-field studies / Figures 3-5: both hemispheres use message-level context, but left-biased processing shows stronger anticipatory feature preparation whereas right-biased processing is more tied to bottom-up fit/plausibility

Psychophysiology 44(4), published pp.500-502, PARLO framework and Conclusions: top-down versus feed-forward hemispheric asymmetry is proposed as an explanatory framework; predictive and integrative strategies may operate in parallel and be recruited dynamically according to resources and task demands

institutions: Department of Psychology, Program in Neuroscience, and Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology, University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign

conditions: preceding sentence or discourse information provides graded constraint over likely upcoming linguistic input
the reviewed anticipation effects are most clearly observed in young adults when contextual support is strong
the actual continuation can match the most expected item, be unexpected while sharing features with it, or be unexpected and feature-dissimilar
resource availability, adult age, and initial hemispheric routing can change the relative contribution of anticipatory versus post-input integration strategies
population: younger and older adult human language comprehenders across the reviewed reading and listening studies
substrate: left-biased and right-biased cerebral processing systems as compared in lateralized-input studies
task: read or listen to constraining language and process expected or unexpected continuations while time-locked scalp electrical responses or related online measures are recorded
temporal_scope: context is available before the critical continuation and can preactivate features before the item is encountered
an early response to the continuation indexes access/facilitation related to prior support, whereas a later frontal response can follow a strongly violated expectation
the source treats anticipatory and integrative processing as potentially concurrent and dynamically weighted rather than as mutually exclusive fixed stages

nodes.description: sentence- or discourse-level information available before the critical continuation
strength with which the preceding context favors a particular continuation or small set of continuations
graded expectation for a particular likely upcoming continuation derived from the preceding context
semantic, morpho-syntactic, lexical, or perceptual properties activated before the corresponding upcoming item is actually presented
the word, article, adjective, or picture actually encountered after the constraining context
degree to which an unexpected continuation shares relevant properties with the contextually favored but unpresented completion
plausibility or fit of the actually presented continuation with the preceding message-level context
centroparietal negative-going response around several hundred milliseconds whose amplitude is reduced when meaning-related information is easier to access
slow frontally distributed positive response selectively enhanced when an unrelated unexpected continuation follows a strongly constraining context
processing mode in which context is used before input arrival to prepare properties of likely upcoming items
processing mode in which the actually presented item is evaluated primarily for its bottom-up fit with the current message representation
age- and resource-related profile associated with differences in the tendency or efficacy of anticipatory processing
ability to rapidly generate words from category or letter cues, which covaries with younger-like anticipation effects among older adults
lateralized visual presentation that initially biases processing toward one cerebral hemisphere
reviewed sentence-completion, category-violation, anticipatory form-cue, age-comparison, and visual-half-field paradigms that contrast context-derived expectations with actual continuations

relations.description: preceding language information establishes a graded expectation over likely upcoming continuations
when an anticipatory strategy is engaged, the favored continuation can preactivate semantic and other item properties before the item appears
the early continuation-evoked response reflects both support for the presented item and, critically, facilitation from properties shared with a strongly expected but unpresented completion
stronger contextual constraint can strengthen advance preparation of features associated with the favored continuation
when an unrelated unexpected continuation violates a strong contextual expectation, a later frontal positive response is enhanced relative to the same unexpected continuation after weak constraint
the late response is associated by the source with consequences of disconfirming a strong expectation, although its exact cognitive and neural mechanism remains unresolved
older adults as a group are less likely or less effective at using context to preactivate properties of upcoming items, despite retaining sensitivity to contextual fit
among older adults, greater rapid word-generation fluency predicts a more younger-like electrophysiological pattern indicative of anticipatory feature use

lateralized-input studies show relatively stronger anticipatory feature preparation after initial left-biased routing and relatively stronger bottom-up plausibility-based processing after initial right-biased routing
the review distinguishes advance context-driven preparation from post-input assessment of the presented item's fit, while allowing both strategies to contribute during normal comprehension
the reviewed context/continuation manipulations expose temporally separable facilitation and expectation-violation consequences
engagement and expression of advance preparation depend on contextual support and differ with resource/age profile and hemispheric processing conditions
